title: Geometric stalks
statement:
Let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. A *pointed etale neighbourhood* of $\bar
t$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ with $U\to T$ an object of the small etale site
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ a lift
of $\bar t$. For a sheaf $F$ on $T_{\Et}$, define its *stalk at $\bar t$* by

$$
 F_{\bar t}=\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)}F(U),
$$

where the colimit runs over pointed etale neighbourhoods with the opposite
index category.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.pointSmallEtale s).sheafFiber.obj F. EtalePoint.lean:64-65 defines the fibre as lifts Spec Omega -> U over s; Point/Basic.lean:96-97 defines its presheaf fibre as colim over the opposite category of elements, and :277-278 restricts this to sheaves. No comparison theorem is needed.

split_report.summary: Mathlib's Scheme.pointSmallEtale packages lifts to etale neighbourhoods as a site point, and GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiber takes the colimit of sections over its opposite category of elements. Together they give the stated geometric stalk directly. The slopmaster2 source has no declaration tagged for this node, and its EtalePoint extension treats both definitions as Mathlib imports.

lean.note: The stalk F_t̄ of a sheaf F on T_Et at a geometric point t̄ : Spec Ω → T is ((pointSmallEtale t̄).sheafFiber).obj F: pointSmallEtale (Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.EtalePoint:64) is the point of smallEtaleTopology T whose fibre at U is the set of lifts Spec Ω → U over t̄, and Point.sheafFiber (Point/Basic.lean:277) is the colimit of F over the opposite category of elements of that fibre, i.e. over pointed etale neighbourhoods. This is the form used by the landed siblings (lean/Sheaf/AlgebraicGeometry/EtaleSupport.lean, EtaleSheaves.lean, GeometricStalkColimits.lean, AbelianSheavesGModules.lean). The node's notion.
